absent: Machine-specific shutdown, protection, and transfer semantics for crash entry
Layout and lifetime of crash image, resource tree root, and per-processor note storage beyond observed fields
Configuration and policy inputs such as deferred notifier mode, panic on fault, and reservation extents
Absolute on-disk locations of routed fragments
Architecture-specific population, exclusion, and hotplug refresh behavior
Full semantics of panic serialization primitives and memory and processor notifier frameworks

findings.text: Predicate that decides whether the current panic context should transfer to a crash kernel immediately, deferring when deferred-after-notifiers mode is enabled and otherwise requesting transfer for interrupt context, idle task, global init, or panic-on-fault policy.
Presence test reporting whether crash image storage currently holds a loaded image.

Crash entry that serializes against concurrent load activity and, when an image is present, captures register state, refreshes diagnostic information, shuts down machine state, allows pending direct memory activity to settle, and transfers control to the stored image before releasing serialization.

Single-word atomic flag providing mutual exclusion between image load or update paths and crash entry, with nonblocking acquire on expected clear state and release to clear state using acquire and release ordering.

Crash size query, memory shrink, hotplug check, and hotplug update paths all attempt the same nonblocking acquire and skip or report inaccuracy when busy, holding it across inspection or mutation of crash image state and releasing on every exit.

Diagnostic note refresh that is a no-op without allocated note storage, optionally switches to a safe copy of the payload, stamps current wall-clock crash time into the payload, and rebuilds the note wrapper in place.

Variable-length note layout with header carrying name length including terminator, payload length, and type, followed by name bytes then payload bytes, each section advanced to word granularity, terminated by an all-zero header.

Formatted diagnostic append that renders into bounded temporary storage, copies only what fits into shared payload at current length, advances length by copied amount, and emits a one-time warning when capacity is reached with truncation.

Externally callable crash handler, also exposed as kernel function for tracing programs, that allows only the first arriving central processor to proceed into crash entry and then restores panic state so later panic calls may retry.

Builder that allocates a zeroed buffer for a core-style header describing per-processor notes, diagnostic note, optional kernel text mapping, and supplied memory ranges, failing allocation cleanly and returning buffer address and total length on success.

Header population assigns note type to per-processor and diagnostic entries with physical addresses and fixed note sizes, assigns load type to kernel text and memory ranges with readable writable executable permissions and identity offset mapping, and counts every emitted entry.

Crash header claims core file type, current version, native architecture and native object ABI, wide class with little-endian encoding, and standard magic with zeroed padding, with header and program entry sizes and offsets set consistently.
Program entries use note type for register and diagnostic data and load type for kernel text and RAM ranges, with permission flags expressing read plus write plus execute.

Range-list subtraction that removes an inclusive interval from a sorted list, deleting fully covered entries, trimming partially overlapped ends, and splitting straddled entries when spare capacity remains, stopping early once sorted order proves no further overlap.

Memory range list is maintained in ascending order, which the exclusion routine relies upon to skip preceding entries and to terminate the scan when the doomed interval ends before the next entry starts.
Splitting a straddled range requires spare list capacity and reports resource exhaustion without mutation when full, while other overlap shapes mutate in place and always succeed.

High-level preparation that queries required range capacity, allocates flexible range storage, populates it by architecture code, excludes reserved crash regions and architecture-specific ranges, optionally reports resulting count for hotplug use, delegates to header builder, and frees temporary storage on every path.
Architecture hooks provide weak defaults reporting no ranges, population failure, successful no-op exclusion, and delegation to generic range exclusion, allowing platforms to override.
Range container allocation zeroes flexible storage sized for requested maximum and records that maximum with initially empty use count implied by zeroing.
Test-only constructor that validates requested capacity against initial use, allocates zeroed flexible storage, records capacity and use counts, and copies supplied initial intervals when present.

Reservation filter that removes the main crash kernel extent, the optional low extent when present, and every contiguous-memory reservation from the candidate dump list, propagating the first exclusion failure.
Size query that attempts nonblocking serialization, sums the main and low reservation sizes treating empty extents as zero, releases serialization, and reports busy when the lock is contended.

Reservation shrink that rounds the request to required granularity, rejects growth while accepting an unchanged size as success, refuses to shrink while an image is loaded, releases trailing memory back to the general resource tree as busy system memory, and collapses the low reservation into the main slot when the main slot becomes empty.
Global resource tree is mutated only under write-mode hold of a dedicated read-write lock, with release and conflict-checked insertion acquiring and releasing around the underlying tree walk.
Resource nodes form a sorted tree linked by parent, child, and sibling pointers with start and end bounds, where siblings are ordered by address and children are fully contained within the parent.

Leaf insertion that validates the new interval against the root bounds and sibling order, splices it into address order when a gap is found, and otherwise returns the conflicting node without mutation.

Subtree insertion that descends while the new interval fully contains successive conflicts, rejects partial overlap or duplicate insertion, and otherwise grafts the covered sibling run beneath the new node while preserving sibling order.
Public insertion wrappers returning success when no conflict exists, with one variant returning the conflicting node for diagnosis and the other translating any conflict into a busy failure.

Removal that unlinks the target from its parent list and either discards its subtree link or re-parents children to the grandparent, clearing the removed parent pointer and reporting invalid argument when the node is not found.

Insertion assumes ordered non-overlapping siblings and rejects out-of-bounds or partially overlapping requests without mutation, while release assumes a valid parent link and leaves the tree unchanged when the target is absent.

Per-processor register capture that validates processor index and note storage, zeroes a status record, stamps current task identity, copies register state, and writes a single status note followed by a terminator.

Early initialization allocates per-processor note buffers sized for one note buffer each, with alignment rounded up to a power of two bounded by page size and a compile-time check that the buffer fits within a single page, warning and failing cleanly on allocation failure.

Hotplug check and update paths serialize on a dedicated mutex outer lock combined with the nonblocking kexec flag inner lock, always releasing in reverse order and treating inner contention as a possibly inaccurate image rather than a hard failure.
Support query that holds both hotplug and kexec serialization while reading the loaded image flag, reporting unsupported when no image is present and releasing both locks on every path.

Hotplug update locates the header segment by scanning for magic when not yet cached, temporarily removes crash-range protection, marks the current hotplug action for architecture code, invokes the architecture handler, then clears the action, records that the header was refreshed, and restores protection, with callback errors never triggering rollback.
Hotplug updates are skipped when no crash image is loaded or when the image disallows hotplug refresh, and the header scan failure is logged and abandoned without invoking architecture code.

Memory online and offline notifications and processor online and offline transitions all funnel into the same hotplug update with distinct action codes and either supplied context or no context, always reporting successful handling to the notifier core.

Early registration that subscribes to memory notifications when that feature is enabled and installs processor transition callbacks when that feature is enabled, returning the processor registration status.
Contiguous-memory settle helper that is a no-op when no such ranges exist and otherwise waits for a fixed timeout to allow in-flight direct memory activity to drain.
Diagnostic prefix for hotplug-related messages identifying the crash hotplug subsystem.
Crash entry silently skips transfer when serialization is contended or no image is present, ensuring panic paths never block on kexec activity.
